title: TypeScript SDK: polymorphic validators + progressive streaming parsers for structured output
creator: Asha Patel
description: Create a cohesive TypeScript SDK flow that generates runtime validators and progressive parsers for polymorphic (tagged/discriminated) output shapes. Goals: 1) Make generated clients expose a stable TypeScript type + Zod validator pair for each model variant. 2) Provide a streaming-friendly parser that can incrementally validate/rehydrate partial tokens for long streaming responses (e.g., chat with embedded structured objects). 3) Emit JSON Schema annotations for integration with downstream tooling (docs, console validation, QA). This ticket covers design, codegen changes, runtime helpers, tests, and initial rollout flag.
acceptance_criteria: Codegen emits a union type and an associated Zod schema for each top-level polymorphic output; consuming apps can import both.
Runtime SDK exposes parseStream(stream) that yields validated objects as they become parsable without buffering entire output for typical chat/stream sizes.
When a streamed chunk cannot be validated yet, parser buffers minimal context and resumes validation once enough tokens arrive (no full-stream buffering for common cases).
Fallback mapping exists: if validation fails for a variant, SDK maps to a generic `UnknownOutput` with source metadata and exposes a `validationErrors` helper.
Generated JSON Schema files are saved alongside types (for console / docs ingestion) and pass round-trip checks with our schema-linting CI job.
End-to-end tests covering streaming with interleaved text + structured objects and offline codegen unit tests present in CI.
Performance: streaming parser does not increase median token latency by >6% on microbenchmarks (see bench links).
technical_notes: Design constraints: many models emit partial JSON fragments during streaming; naive JSON.parse-per-chunk is unsafe. We need a progressive, tolerant decoder that reassembles bracketed regions and validates only completed JSON objects.

We prefer Zod for runtime validation since it's already used in other SDK parts; however, Zod has limitations validating incremental fragments. Plan: generate per-variant partial schemas and use a small progressive collector to feed completed fragments into Zod.parse.

To support JSON Schema emission, we will add an optional codegen step that maps our type-level metadata into draft-07 JSON Schema. Keep mapping rules simple (no oneOf/anyOf explosion) using explicit discriminator fields where possible.
Memory trade-off: buffering minimal JSON object fragments vs. simplicity of buffering whole response. Aim to keep typical working set < 8KB for chat-like interleaving.

Fallback behavior: when parse/validation fails after a timeout threshold, tag object as `UnknownOutput` and attach raw string + parse error for user inspection. This keeps caller apps resilient to model regressions.
Rollout plan: behind feature flag `enablePolymorphicValidators`; initial rollout to 5% of SDK users, then 25% after soak. Desktop SDK versions will be flagged for breaking change notes.
implementation_plan: Design doc: store in Drive -> /Design/ts-sdk/polymorphic-validators-2025-02-17 (link below).
Codegen: update ts-codegen module to emit <Type>.ts (types) + <Type>.schema.ts (Zod) + <Type>.schema.json (JSON Schema).
Runtime: add `ParseStream` helper class in SDK runtime that stitches bracketed fragments, extracts candidate objects, and calls generated Zod validators.
CLI: add `--emit-json-schema` flag to the SDK generator, default off for backwards compatibility.
Tests: unit tests for codegen output, integration tests against a fake streaming model that intermittently emits pieces of JSON, e2e test for Node and Deno runtimes.
Benchmarks: microbench harness to measure parser overhead; add to perf CI and verify <6% median token latency increase.
Docs & Examples: Add a 'streaming structured output' example in SDK examples folder plus a migration guide for existing TS users.
PRs: create phasable PRs—codegen changes, runtime helper, tests, docs. Ensure each PR small and reviewable.
test_plan: Unit tests for generated Zod schemas: property-level positive/negative cases per variant.
Streaming integration test: fake stream that yields: ""
Edge-case test: object split across multiple small chunks with noise between objects.
Recovery test: intentionally corrupt a variant and assert SDK returns UnknownOutput with validationErrors attached.
Performance test: run on CI perf runner and assert parser overhead < +6% median token latency; regression alerts on failure.
